page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; marginal notes in the right margin and a few short notes in the left margin; running head at top; page number 681 at top right; signature Vv 5 at foot.

main_text.p: Septentrionali Hyrcania, Hijahan, Kom, Adiarbigan & Armenia, Occiduo Babylonia & Irach, obvenirent) devitae multos Philosophorum etiam Indicorum libros, (inter quos Kelilah, Il Sudemana) in Persicum idioma transferri curavit, & Scachi-ludum ab inventoribus Indis, primum accepit.

In ARABIA FELICE fuere post Hamyarum Hiskar F & Abrahah Alsabah I. Sharahe, Ius Hammer, Dhu Jadan & Zara Dhu Nuwas, & ex Abyssinis Aryath, Abrahah Ashram, & post Jaf (sum, Abraha F. Mhaban in bello contra Mauritaniam cecidit. Alii ci Ebn Dahr, cui pene infinitus ille Amri Ebn Maadi Carb: gladius, Mahoma dictus, erat Dhu Shanatir, cognomen- to Lachtaal, pueros nobiles, & puellas regiae filiis, turpi cum dehonestaret libidine a fuccessore quem multebri patientiae subjicere voluit, in Ecostrali obtruncatus est. Dhu Jadan i.e. voce Adana praeditus, ultimus a quibusdam Hamyarium Regum putatur, Ahmed Ebn Yulef conjadicente. Zara Dhunuas (sn Dhu Nuwas, a cinis a tergo pendulis ita dictus, Jujipu alias, & Dominus fovea, quod omnes Judaismum profiteri assultantes in ignem accensum conjiciebantur, & Christianos percucerunt. Motum ideo illi ab Abyssinis bellum, Duce Arbate, quo victo, & regno subjugato, pervenit imperium ad Aethiopes, quorum primus Arbata, seu, ut alii vocant, Ariath, a fuccessore per invidiam obtruncatus est. Abrahah Alahram a cicatrice vulneris, in- fucle inflicti, ita denominatus est, nec non Domi- nus Elephantis, de qua re fabellam apud Pococki- um.

page.notes: Transcription is partly uncertain: the page is heavily damaged and show-through from the reverse side is present. Marginal notes on the right are faint and largely illegible; the Hebrew/Arabic-style names and several Latin words are reconstructed with [?] where unreadable. Page number 681 and running head are printed at the top.
